title: Preoxygenation in Bronchoscopy during conscious sedation (PreBRO)
summary:
This study is being carried out to investigate whether oxygen administration at the beginning of the examination without proven oxygen deficiency leads to less drop in oxygen saturation. For this purpose, participating patients are treated with oxygen in one group and with compressed air in the other group. In both groups, administration to the patient and investigator will be performed at low flow (2 L/min). The allocation to the groups is carried out randomly (so-called randomization). All patients will be treated if there is a drop in oxygen after discontinuation of sedative medication and ensuring a patent airway.
Oxygen can also have undesirable effects, e.g. B Drying of the mucous membrane, nosebleeds, impairment of communication and food intake through masks and tubes and, in some patients with lung disease, also lead to an increase in carbon dioxide in the blood. Compressed air can also dry out the mucous membrane and is also given via a probe/nasal cannula.
 The study aims to gain insight into whether oxygen therapy is even necessary in preparation for a bronchoscopy

interventions.name: Insufflation of 2L/min pressured air before and during bronchoscopy
Insufflation of 2L/min oxygen before and during bronchoscopy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Adult patients 18 years and older
•	Indication for flexible bronchoscopy with conscious sedation
•	Written consent
•	Arterial or capillary blood gas analysis on room air available in last  72 hour before bronchoscopy
Exclusion criteria:
•	SpO2 or /SaO2 < 92% on room air
•	Artificial airway
•	FEV1 < 1,0 L
•	BMI > 40 kg/m2
•	pH < 7.35
.- planned   Argon-Plasma or electrocoagulation
•	Continuous need for oxygen (long term oxygen therapy)
•	Need for non-invasive ventilation
•	Use of i.v. vasopressors, inotropes or systolic BP < 90 mm Hg
•	Myocardial infarction within previous 28 days
•	Stroke within previous 28 days
•	Mechanical respiratory support (invasive mechanical ventilation, ECMO)
•	Epilepsy with seizure within last 12 months
•	Use of illicit drugs
•	Comorbidity with estimated life expectancy < 6 months
•	Dementia or inability to communicate
•	Lack of informed consent
